title: Restriction and extension by zero for modules on a localized site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $U$ be an object, and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Give $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topology and write $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal C)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O|_U}(\mathcal C/U)$ for the categories of sheaves of modules [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_U^*:\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O|_U}(\mathcal C/U)$ be restriction, $G\mapsto G|_U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and for a sheaf $F$ of $\mathcal O|_U$-modules let $j_{U!}F=P_F^\#$ be the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of its extension-by-zero presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $P_F$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], functorial in $F$ (the *extension by zero*). Then $j_U^*$ is an exact functor, and $j_{U!}$ is an exact functor left adjoint to it: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(j_{U!}F,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O|_U}(F,j_U^*G)$ naturally in the $\mathcal O|_U$-module $F$ and the $\mathcal O$-module $G$.

proof.text: Restriction is the sectionwise functor overFunctor of the localized ringed site. Extension is the direct-sum presheaf extension followed by the module sheafification. Both functors retain independent object and morphism universes; coefficients and modules live in max c v r.

For a map from the extension presheaf to G, precompose its section at V with the linear injection of the summand indexed by V → U. In the reverse direction apply DirectSum.toModule to the slice components of a map F → G|U. The restriction formula on each summand proves naturality, DirectSum.toModule.unique proves the first inverse law, and DirectSum.toModule_lof proves the second. Verify naturality in both module sheaves on summand generators. Compose with sheafificationHomEquiv and apply Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv. Its unit is definitionally the prescribed summand injection followed by the sheafification unit. Any other adjunction with that formula has equal units componentwise, hence is equal by Adjunction.ext.

Restriction is additive componentwise, so its constructed left adjoint is additive by Adjunction.left_adjoint_additive. The adjunction supplies colimit preservation by extension and limit preservation by restriction. A monomorphism of slice module sheaves is injective on sections because evaluation preserves finite limits. DirectSum.lmap_injective makes its extension-presheaf map injective on every section; PresheafOfModules.mono_of_injective makes this map mono. Module sheafification preserves finite limits and therefore monomorphisms. Thus the extension preserves monomorphisms and cokernels. Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesMonos_and_cokernels and Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology give its finite-limit preservation.

The forgetful functor from module sheaves preserves finite colimits by moduleSheaves_colimits_forgetful. Underlying abelian sheaves commute definitionally with restriction to the slice. The forgetful site functor Over.forget U is continuous and cocontinuous; Mathlib sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous makes its abelian-sheaf restriction a left adjoint and hence colimit preserving. Therefore module restriction followed by forgetting preserves finite colimits. Since the faithful module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms and preserves finite colimits, it reflects finite colimits. Apply preservesFiniteColimits_of_reflects_of_preserves to conclude right exactness of module restriction.
